obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1, assessed as a service provider
citation: PCI SSC PCI DSS v4.0.1 (June 2024); card brand rules through the sponsor agreement
basis: The company stores, processes and transmits cardholder data for its merchants and is registered with the card brands as the sponsor bank's third-party processor. At about 95 million transactions a year it is Level 1 under Visa's service provider levels (more than 300,000), so it validates with an annual ROC by a QSA

obligation: FTC Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information (Safeguards Rule)
basis: A non-bank financial institution under FTC jurisdiction: data processing of financial data is listed in 12 CFR 225.28(b)(14). The rule covers customer information of other financial institutions' customers (314.1(b)), and the token vault holds data on far more than 5,000 consumers, so the 314.6 exception does not apply

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule: bank service provider notice (OCC)
basis: The sponsor agreement states that settlement, reconciliation and merchant funding file services are performed for the national bank and are subject to examination under 12 U.S.C. 1867(c). They are covered services (53.2(b)(5)), so the company is a bank service provider (53.2(b)(2))

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule: bank service provider notice (FDIC and Federal Reserve)
basis: No covered services are performed for an FDIC-supervised or Board-supervised organization. The letter of intent with an FDIC-supervised state nonmember bank has no services under it; 304.24 applies once that sponsor agreement is signed (target 2027-Q1)

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
basis: The Guidelines apply to the sponsor bank. They reach the company only through the sponsor agreement's service provider oversight terms (Guidelines III.D)

obligation: NCUA cyber incident reporting
basis: Not a credit union and serves none

obligation: SEC Regulation SCI
basis: Not an SCI entity

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation
basis: The company holds no New York license, registration or charter, so the 500.19(a) exemption analysis is not reached

obligation: CIRCIA (pending rule)
basis: No final rule; tracked for planning

obligation: SEC public-company cybersecurity disclosure
basis: Not an SEC registrant

obligation: Bank Service Company Act examination of services
basis: The sponsor agreement makes the settlement and funding services subject to examination by the bank's regulator

obligation: Card brand incident rules (Visa What To Do If Compromised) and the sponsor agreement's 24-hour notice
citation: Visa Core Rules and supplements; sponsor agreement
basis: The company processes Visa account data for the sponsor bank's merchants; the sponsor agreement requires notice of any suspected account data compromise within 24 hours

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification)
basis: The company holds personal information of Florida residents: as a third-party agent of its merchants for cardholder data (501.171(6)) and as a covered entity for merchant owner data

obligation: Breach notification laws of each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Merchants are located in 41 states and cardholders nationwide

obligation: PCI PIN Security Requirements
basis: The company does not process PIN transactions and holds no PIN keys

obligation: State money transmission licensing
basis: Merchant funds settle through the sponsor bank's accounts

obligation: Federal contract cyber clauses (Section 889 and Kaspersky)
basis: The company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices), applied to AI claims and outcomes
basis: Claims to merchants about the fraud model and unjustified decline outcomes for cardholders fall under Section 5

obligation: Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B
basis: The company is not a creditor and does not decide on credit; issuers make the credit authorization decision

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (automated decision technology)
applies: To be assessed by counsel by 2026-12-15
basis: Merchants are located in 41 states. Whether an automatic fraud decline of a purchase is a consequential decision about a financial service is not settled
